questions.prompt: After Chapter 10 designs a coherent whole, what does Chapter 11 add?
choices: How to concentrate effort where it matters most
How to support every priority equally
How to avoid strategic tradeoffs
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 moves from coherence to concentration, asking where effort should be placed most heavily.

questions.prompt: What does focus mean in this chapter?
choices: Personal motivation and steady willpower
Concentrating effort where it can create the strongest effect
Giving identical support to all worthwhile priorities
questions.explanation: Focus is strategic concentration under limits, not generic discipline or equal distribution.

choices: Accepting uneven emphasis where it matters
Assuming broad but thin support is strong enough
Choosing a few priorities for heavier backing
questions.explanation: The chapter warns that diffusion can leave a coherent strategy too weak on every front.

questions.prompt: A school team spreads equal attention across many projects and none of them improves much. What is the Chapter 11 diagnosis?
choices: The plan needs more worthy priorities
The effort is diffusing too broadly
The team should avoid concentration
questions.explanation: Diffusion spreads support across too many priorities so none gets enough force to matter.

questions.prompt: Why do constraints make focus necessary?
choices: Because finite attention and resources punish broad spread
Because constraints remove the need for choice
Because all priorities become equally important
questions.explanation: Real limits mean extra effort has to be concentrated where it will create the strongest result.

choices: By replacing design with generic discipline
By deciding where the designed whole should concentrate force
By treating coherence as enough on its own
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 builds a coherent whole; Chapter 11 asks where that whole should place its heaviest emphasis.

questions.prompt: A home project only starts moving after one goal receives most of the available effort. What concept is this showing?
choices: Selective intensity
Average coverage
Avoidance of tradeoffs
questions.explanation: The project improves because effort is concentrated where it can have the biggest effect.

questions.prompt: What is the best sign that a strategy is diffusing effort too widely?
choices: Several priorities stay alive but none gains enough force to matter
One priority carries clearly heavier backing
The plan accepts uneven emphasis
questions.explanation: Diffusion keeps many priorities active while leaving each one strategically underpowered.

questions.prompt: Why can equal support weaken a strategy?
choices: Because fairness is always wrong
Because spreading force evenly can leave every priority too weak
Because only one priority should ever exist
questions.explanation: The chapter argues that equal support can thin the whole strategy until no aim gets enough emphasis to matter.

questions.prompt: Why does Chapter 11 naturally lead into later growth questions?
choices: Because concentrated force changes how expansion should be judged
Because growth removes the need for focus
Because every expansion preserves force automatically
questions.explanation: Once force is concentrated, later strategy has to ask whether expansion will preserve that strength or dilute it.
